sonnet.problem: No story card has set up Ephesus or Paul leaving Priscilla and Aquila behind. Card 3 ends with them sailing for Syria. A baker has nothing to reason from here, so the pick is luck.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. **The check:** could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: Apollos's decision to cross over to Achaia is never set up on a story card before this question. Card 6 is a choice card, and the setup was not already told. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason whether the brothers would try to talk him out of it.
sonnet.rule: Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

sonnet.problem: The card calls the brothers' writing a "letter of recommendation." Verse 27 only says they "wrote to the disciples there to welcome him." The card renames what the text describes.
sonnet.rule: **Call things what the text calls them.** ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)
